description: Tracing an inbound HTTPS request from an external web client through the management cluster's ingress proxy, across the OVS overlay fabric, into the KubeVirt VM, and down to the front-end workload Pod.

steps.description: Client sends HTTPS request to the Route hostname. The Shared Ingress Proxy (HAProxy) in the management cluster terminates TLS and identifies the guest cluster backend.
HAProxy forwards the decrypted request into the management worker node's OVS br-int bridge, which applies OVN flow rules to route the packet toward the KubeVirt Launcher.
OVS routes the packet through the tap0 virtual interface into the KubeVirt Launcher Pod, crossing the host-to-VM network boundary.
The KubeVirt Launcher delivers the packet to the virtio-net NIC of the Guest Worker Node VM, shifting context from the host kernel to the guest RHCOS kernel.
The guest RHCOS kernel hands the packet to the in-VM Open vSwitch service, which evaluates guest OVN flow rules to identify the target workload Pod.
Guest OVS delivers the packet to the OpenShift Ingress Router Pod running inside the VM, which re-routes it to the correct guest Service endpoint.
The guest Ingress Router forwards the request to the Front-End Workload Pod via its ClusterIP Service. The application process accepts the connection and returns a response.

description: Tracing how a new workload Pod is scheduled and started in the guest cluster: from a kubectl apply hitting the Guest API Server through scheduling, kubelet notification, and CRI-O container creation inside the Guest VM.

steps.description: Developer runs 'oc apply -f deployment.yaml'. The request reaches the Guest API Server, which validates it, persists the Deployment to etcd, and notifies controllers via watch events.
The Guest Scheduler watches for Pods with no node assignment. It evaluates guest worker node capacity and affinity rules, then selects the Guest Worker Node VM.
The Scheduler writes a Binding object back to the Guest API Server, officially assigning the Pod to the Guest Worker Node.
The Guest API Server needs to notify the guest kubelet inside the VM. The notification travels through the Konnectivity Server tunnel in the management cluster.
The Konnectivity Server relays the PodSpec through the persistent tunnel to the Konnectivity Agent running inside the Guest Worker Node VM.
The Konnectivity Agent delivers the PodSpec to the guest kubelet. Kubelet validates the spec and instructs guest CRI-O to pull the image and create the container.
Guest CRI-O receives a RunPodSandbox and CreateContainer gRPC call, pulls the image, sets up the cgroup hierarchy, and invokes the CNI plugin to provision the Pod's network namespace.
Guest CRI-O starts the container via runc. The workload process becomes PID 1 inside its namespaces, registers with the guest network, and the Pod transitions to Running status.

description: Tracing how the HyperShift Operator bootstraps a new Hosted Control Plane: creating the guest control-plane namespace, launching the Guest API Server and etcd, and establishing the Konnectivity tunnel to the first worker node.

steps.description: Platform admin applies a HostedCluster manifest via 'oc apply'. The Management API Server persists it and notifies the HyperShift Operator.
The HyperShift Operator reconciles the HostedCluster CR and begins provisioning: it creates the Dedicated Guest Control Plane Namespace and populates it with control-plane Deployments.
HyperShift deploys the Etcd StatefulSet in the guest namespace. Once etcd is healthy and a quorum is established, the Guest API Server is allowed to start.
HyperShift deploys the Konnectivity Server. It starts listening for inbound tunnel connections from worker node agents before nodes are provisioned.
HyperShift starts the Ignition Server to serve bootstrap configuration payloads to new worker nodes as they boot for the first time.
The first Guest Worker Node VM boots and fetches its Ignition config from the Ignition Server over TLS. The config contains kubelet certificates and bootstrap manifests.
Once RHCOS boots inside the VM, the Konnectivity Agent starts and opens an outbound persistent tunnel to the Konnectivity Server in the management cluster.
With the tunnel established, the guest kubelet starts and registers the node with the Guest API Server. The guest control plane is now fully operational.
